title: Give job introspections the unmet criteria, findings and failed checks
summary: When a rejected or failed job is introspected, build the event's `what` from the job's verification.json (unmet criteria, blocker/major findings, failed checks with their names) instead of only the title and outcome reason. The model then stops saying the stored fields omit them and no longer files a failed test check as an unmet criterion. The audience is the steward and the person reading introspections to group rejections by real cause.

defaults_applied.how: Fix the input the model is given, not the six records or the wording of one prompt.
Unit tests for the three job shapes; test, clippy, fmt must pass.
A behavior criterion exercises the prompt built from a real-shaped rejection.
One focused change in introspect.rs plus changelog.
The sources are enforced in code, with tests, not by prompt prose alone.
Docs and comments written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The root cause is that event_of_job builds `what` from only the title and outcome.reason, so the model never sees verification.json; the fix is to read it there (JobRecords already has a `verification: Option<Verification>` field).
Surfacing failed checks separately addresses the misfiling of job 20261014-221551-09t4's test failure as an unmet criterion.
The module doc's 'reads only the stored fields it lists' rule is extended to name these verification fields; transcripts and diffs stay excluded.
The schema athena.introspection/1 needs no change since the extra information lives in the existing `what` input.

acceptance_criteria.text: event_of_job in crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs reads the job's stored Verification and puts each unmet criterion's text and each blocker or major finding (severity, summary, location) into the Event's `what`; the field list in the module docs (and defaults-loop.md section 3.3 if it lists fields) names these additions.

A failed check (CheckRun with passed=false) is rendered in `what` under a separate, explicitly labelled 'failed checks' heading with its name and a bounded output_tail, never in the unmet-criteria list; the system prompt tells the model that criteria and checks are different things.

Added text is bounded (counts and character caps), redacted like the rest of the prompt, and still excludes transcripts, diffs and other jobs' files; a job with no verification.json (e.g. failed before verification) still produces the old `what`.

New unit tests in introspect.rs cover: a rejection with one unmet criterion and a major finding (both appear in the prompt), a rejection whose only failure is a failed test check (appears as failed check, no unmet criterion), and a job without verification. Run `cargo test -p athena-core introspect`; `cargo test` passes, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` are clean.

Outcome check for the steward: with the fake model, the user prompt for a rejected job built from a verification.json like that of job 20261014-170031-2r9b contains the text of the unmet criterion 8 and the major finding location, so a reader of the resulting introspection need not say 'the stored fields do not name them'.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or re-running the six existing introspection records
Adding verification data to the rejection outcome.json itself
Changing Jev shadow behaviour or the introspection schema
